page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c4.xlarge is a compute-focused instance within the High Clock Speed family, powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor with a base clock frequency of 3.2 GHz. The instance allocates 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores across 2 threads per core, paired with 8.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU). It includes 25 MB of L3 cache, alongside 32 KB of L1 data cache and 0.25 MB of L2 cache per core. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, but newer instructions such as AVX-512 and AMX are not supported.

Hardware bundling does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators, meaning persistent storage must be attached over the network. Baseline network throughput is rated at 2 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provided with the instance.

Performance benchmarks place this instance predominantly in the lower quartile of modern cloud servers due to the older Broadwell microarchitecture. Its Geekbench single-core score of 1115.0 and multi-core score of 2416.0 reflect lower overall throughput compared to modern architectures. Large-block memory reads achieve 22.04 GB/sec, while write operations reach 14.84 GB/sec. Compression metrics present mixed outcomes: single-threaded gzip compression performs in the middle 50% tier at 25.81 GB/sec, whereas multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 17.93 GB/sec, falling into the bottom 10%.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the ecs.c4.xlarge offers dedicated compute resources suitable for legacy x86 compute workloads, lightweight batch processing, small-scale web serving (reaching 4.08 GB/sec in static web tests), and modest key-value caching workloads, generating 3.38 million Redis SET operations per second.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c4.xlarge is a compute-focused virtual machine from the High Clock Speed family. It features a 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor with 4 dedicated vCPUs (2 physical cores), 8.0 GB of system memory, and a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or GPU acceleration. Benchmarking indicates lower-tier performance against modern hardware generations, recording a PassMark CPU score of 4191.26 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2416.0. Memory bandwidth reaches 22.04 GB/sec on large uncached read operations. The instance is suited for moderate compute tasks, lightweight web serving, and small-scale caching workloads requiring predictable CPU allocation without intensive memory or local storage requirements.
